native_result.query: In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: Between 1500 BCE and 1300 BCE, highest growth of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE is seen.
native_result.HypoB: The highest-growth phase between 2000 and 1100 BCE is the 15th-14th centuries BCE (1500-1300 BCE), peaking in the 15th century BCE (1500-1401 BCE, ~+0.19%/yr growth of the 100-year-smoothed openness score). Landscape openness collapsed to its period minimum around 1500 BCE and then rebounded at the fastest rates of the entire window through 1400-1300 BCE, reaching maximum openness levels around 1300-1200 BCE. This pollen-based growth phase coincides with the broadest rise in capital indicators (symbolic weapons, social house/monument investment, and economic metals/depots all jump into 1400-1301 BCE), although pottery-related (cultural) indicators remain flat - a noted exception - and the latest economic uptick (depot hoards at 1100 BCE) postdates the pollen-growth peak.
